headline: Treat values as next pointers and locate a cycle entrance
statement: nums has n+1 entries, each between 1 and n. Exactly one distinct value appears more than once. Return it without modifying nums and with constant extra space.
constraints: All values lie in [1,n], and exactly one distinct value is repeated.
intuition: Each index points to index nums[index]. Starting at zero eventually enters a cycle because the graph is finite. Zero cannot be a destination. The cycle entrance has two incoming edges along this path, so its index is the repeated value. Floyd's two speeds detect the cycle without a visited set.
approach: Move slow by one edge and fast by two until they meet.
Reset a finder pointer to index zero.
Move finder and slow one edge at a time until they meet.
correctness: Let μ be the path length before the cycle and λ its length. At the first meeting after t slow steps, t is a multiple of λ. Advancing one pointer from zero and the other from the meeting for μ steps makes them meet at the entrance. This entrance has distinct incoming predecessors from the path and cycle, identifying the unique repeated value.
bruteForce: Use a seen set in O(n) space, or compare all pairs in O(n²). Neither meets both requested resource constraints.

complexity.explanation: Cycle detection and entrance search each traverse at most a linear number of edges.

pitfalls: Follow nums[index], rather than incrementing indices.
The repeated value may occur more than twice.
Do not sort or mark nums because mutation is forbidden.
